newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland Cotton sees further growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland Cotton sees further growth.

text.p: Australia's largest ginner and marketer of cotton, Queensland Cotton Holdings Ltd, expects continued growth in the full year to February 28 1997 after a 67 percent jump in net profit to A$10.55 million for the six months to August 31.

Chairman Ben Macdonald said in the half-year report that the company was looking for further growth in its merchandising division for the second half as excellent agronomic conditions provided an ideal market.
The industry was gearing for a strong 1997 season, which would be reflected in the 1998 financial year, he said.

Major increases in production were expected in New South Wales (NSW) because of the available water supply, while the official forecast was for a record Australian crop of 2.25 to 3.0 million bales, he said.

The company's capital expansion over the past few years including the building of a gin and the establishment of a merchandising operation in the Namoi Valley had been designed to benefit from expected increased production in NSW, he said.
Major benefits for the company would be in its marketing and mnerchandising divisions, he said.
"All cotton areas in Queensland except Emerald are facing the best planting conditions for five years, giving us strong optimism in assessing the future of our operations in both states," he said.
The company's record August 31 half-year performance reflected consistent growth in operations across the three divisions of ginning, marketing and merchandising, he said.

The result reflected a combination of strong national cotton production, although at volumes still under industry capacity, successful expansion moves and the efficiency of the company's operations, he said.
Interim dividend has been increased to seven cents a share from five cents a share.
